summary.text: A WWII freighter destroyed in a secret 1944 weapons test, now a Florida Panhandle Shipwreck Trail dive off Pensacola. The scattered wreckage covers a wide stretch of sand, with boilers and plating that hold plenty of fish.

summary.text: A 409 ft former cable ship sunk as a reef in 1988 and later broken into three sections by hurricanes, giving a multi-level wreck dive. Sand tigers often shelter on it.

summary.text: A 328 ft landing craft repair ship sunk in 1992 about 10 miles off Emerald Isle. Shallow enough for long bottom times, it is a popular inshore wreck for novice divers and training.

summary.text: An 1888 passenger steamer lying upright in mud off the Golden Gate in over 200 ft. Cold water and strong currents make it a very experienced-diver-only site; the hull is largely rotted away.

summary.text: A retired Coast Guard cutter, famed for a Perfect Storm rescue, sunk in 2017 as part of the Del-Jersey-Land Inshore Reef about 26-33 nautical miles offshore. Divers can explore its decks and passageways.

summary.text: A flooded Pennsylvania limestone quarry used for training and fun diving, with a school bus, fire engine, aircraft and boats placed between 20 and 100 ft. Visibility and temperature vary with the season.

summary.text: A spring-fed former quarry near Birmingham cut into several levels, popular for training with sunken vehicles and a sailboat. Visibility runs about 25 ft in summer and much better in winter.
